source: Barreiro-Hurle et al. (2021), JRC121368, EUR 30317 EN, doi:10.2760/98160 - F2F + BDS targets scenario, 2030
scenario: all four targets simultaneously (pesticides -50%, nutrient surplus, organic 25%, landscape 10%), CAP 2014-2020 unchanged

published_production_changes_pct.livestock: most heavily impacted within that range

trade_effects: net export position falls for cereals, pork and poultry; trade deficit worsens for oilseeds, fruit and vegetables, beef, sheep and goat meat
citation_of_numbers: Production reductions ~15% cereals, ~15% oilseeds, ~12% fruit/veg/permanent - reported in Journal of Industrial and Business Economics (2025) summarising the JRC data
5-15% decline across all sectors, livestock worst, ~10% producer price rise, -28.4% GHG with CAP LP - Copa-Cogeca commentary on the report
how_to_use: This is a MAGNITUDE benchmark for a full four-target F2F bundle at EU level, comparable in kind to the EcAMPA 2 figures used to validate the carbon MACC.

CAPRI-mod can currently represent landscape elements (SETA floor), the nitrogen ceiling and the organic area target. It CANNOT represent the pesticide target (no PPP cost data). So a like-for-like comparison must either exclude pesticides from CAPRI's bundle or state the omission.

CAPRI's own caveat applies to any comparison: it states production impacts are likely OVERESTIMATED because co-benefits are not modelled, and that magnitudes 'should not be taken as definitive in absolute terms'.
important_caveat_on_our_side: Our GREEN_DEAL_F2F scenario is a PARTIAL bundle. Comparing our partial result against CAPRI's full four-target result would attribute the missing instruments to a wrong economic response. The defensible comparison is instrument-by-instrument where both models represent the instrument.
